extracted.intended_audience: government regulatory analysts and stakeholders (businesses, trade associations, policymakers, public interest groups)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for generating credible estimates of the anticipated costs of individual proposed regulations (before they become final) using the Mercatus Regulatory Cost Calculator; aimed at informing comments, RIAs, and policymaking. Emphasizes identifying both direct and indirect costs and eliciting information economists can use to estimate costs to customers and society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct expenditures on compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct expenditures on compliance, such as paperwork, new equipment, or employee training;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Count explicit monetary outlays businesses incur to comply with a regulation (examples given: paperwork, new equipment, employee training). These are the straightforward, often-invoiced costs the regulation imposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of owner/manager/employee time diverted to regulatory compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The value of owner, manager, or employee time diverted to regulatory compliance;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include opportunity cost of labor time spent on compliance activities (e.g., recordkeeping, meetings, implementation tasks). Monetize by using appropriate wage rates or shadow prices for managerial time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profit forgone on diverted investments
rubrics_metrics.description: Profit forgone on investments the business no longer makes as it is forced to divert resources to regulatory compliance;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture foregone returns from projects or investments not undertaken because resources were reallocated to compliance. This is an opportunity-cost category distinct from direct expenditures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Business profit loss and consumer losses from market responses
rubrics_metrics.description: The profit businesses lose and the value consumers lose from the price increases, quality changes, or other sales-reducing behavioral responses induced by regulation;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for both producer surplus losses and consumer welfare losses resulting from pass-through price increases, reduced product quality, or demand responses. Consider behavioral responses that reduce sales or change market structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Costs of resources spent to influence regulation
rubrics_metrics.description: The costs of resources that businesses and trade associations expend to influence regulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include monetary and time costs devoted to lobbying, comment preparation, litigation planning, trade association activities, or other efforts to influence regulatory outcomes when those are incurred as a response to the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include indirect and non-explicit (opportunity) costs, not just explicit expenditures
rubrics_metrics.description: These costs are not always explicit or obvious, because some of them involve lost opportunities rather than expenditures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the analysis identifies both direct and indirect costs — including lost opportunities and other non-invoiced burdens — rather than limiting scope to easily observed expenditures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elicit information usable by economists to estimate societal costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of the Cost Calculator is to provide better information on the full cost of regulation by identifying both direct and indirect costs and eliciting information that economists can use to estimate the cost of regulation to customers and our broader society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design data collection and responses so they support economic estimation (e.g., provide quantities, prices, timing, behavioral assumptions). Emphasize transparency and documentation so analysts can translate inputs into estimates of costs to customers and society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce accurate, credible estimates before regulations are final
rubrics_metrics.description: The Regulatory Cost Calculator is a practical tool designed to generate better data on the anticipated costs of individual proposed regulations before they become final regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on producing credible, evidence-based estimates during the proposal stage so stakeholders and regulators can use them in notice-and-comment, RIAs, and policy deliberations. Timeliness (pre-final rule) is part of the tool's intended use.
